mention.lead_sentence: The mind map of our study is shown in Figure 1 in detail. Firstly, a new evaluation

items.note: A 435.4x253.2 pt raster flowchart of the whole study, drawn as four dashed 'Step' containers that carry the working chain: 'Superior Indicators' (Food, Society, Efficiency, Economy, Emergency) into 'Identification of Indicators', then 'Basic Food System' and 'Optimization Model' into 'Food system', then two application branches 'Applications in developed countries' and 'Applications in developing countries', then 'Sensitivity Analysis', 'Finding Equilibrium Point' and 'Discussing priorities', with 'Discussing scalability and adaptability' closing. Two side lists spell the equity and sustainability indicator sets (Race, Food Safety, Policy, Gender; Climate Change, Water Use, Land-system Change, N/P flows, Biodiversity). No axis, no number, no legend, no scale, and the whole diagram is one image path, so no label of it exists in the text layer. Printed defects: the 'Step 3' label floats outside its own dashed box with nothing anchoring it, one block lower-cases 'equity' while the block below capitalises 'Equity', and three grey arrows converge on 'Finding Equilibrium Point' with no way to tell which carries which indicator set.

Food carries Food Species, Food Price, Food Production and Food Nutrition; Society carries Population, Age Structure, Food Habits, Education and Health; Emergency carries Accident Disaster, Public Hygiene, Natural Calamities and Social security; Economy and Efficiency carry Urbanization Process, GDP, Consuming Ability, Currency Inflation, Unemployment Rate, Food Packing, Food Storage, Communication Technology, Market Information, Food Processing and Transportation. No axis, no number, no legend beyond the five hub colours, one image path. Printed defects: 'Transportation' breaks across two lines as 'Transporta tion', 'Communication Technology' wraps mid-phrase into the next ring, and 'Social security' lower-cases what every other node capitalises.

The layout measures no equation, no algorithm box and no table-of-contents block here, unlike the previous paper in this block, because every display equation in this PDF is set as text rather than vector strokes. Fifteen of the sixteen figures are image-only, one path each, so no label of them exists in the text layer; the five tables measure from three paths each, being booktabs top, header and bottom rules. Captions are uniform in side and thin in content: every figure caption prints below its drawing, every table caption above its grid, and no caption states a unit, a variable or a reading - the two caption-sharing lines on p16 and p20 ('Figure 9: Greece   Figure 10: Kenya', 'Figure 13: Greece   Figure 14: Kenya') are the extreme case, naming two exhibits in one line with nothing but a country between them. The five tables print only two distinct titles between them. Citation is near-absent: twelve pointer lines in twenty-five pages, four of them numbered (Figure 1, 'figure 2', and Table 2 twice, the last a mis-pointer to content Table 3 holds) and thirteen of the twenty-one exhibits never cited at all. rules: This paper's census closes exactly: 25 pages, 46 measured regions = 25 page-foot stamps plus 21 non-stamp regions, and the paper's text layer prints exactly 21 exhibit captions (Figures 1 to 16 and Tables 1 to 5, no gaps), so the 21 regions are the 21 exhibits one for one and NO region is left over to exclude - the first paper in this block where the exclusion list holds nothing but the page stamps, because this PDF sets its twenty-odd display equations, its algorithm-free body and its table of contents as text with no vector strokes, so they never measure as regions the way they did in #268; [caption.numbering] therefore reads 'Figure N:' sixteen times and 'Table N:' five times.

Caption side is again kind-driven, with no exception: all sixteen figure captions print BELOW their drawing and all five table captions print ABOVE their grid - Figure 1 y754.5 under a raster ending at 749.5, Figure 2 y329.2 under 324.2, Figure 12 y754.5 under 749.5, Figure 15 y750.0 under 745.0, against Table 1 y649.8 over 666.8, Table 2 y75.8 over 92.9, Table 3 y633.6 over 651.6, Table 4 y355.5 over 372.6 and Table 5 y494.4 over 511.4, so [caption.position] is 'below' on every figure row and 'above' on every table row.

Two printed caption LINES carry two labels each, because the paper sets a pair of countries drawings side by side and captions them with one line: p16 prints 'Figure 9: Greece   Figure 10: Kenya' and p20 prints 'Figure 13: Greece   Figure 14: Kenya'. A third pair, Figures 7 and 8 on p16, takes two separate caption lines that happen to print at the same y323.47, one under each raster. So [caption.verbatim] is a bare 'Figure 9: Greece' and 'Figure 10: Kenya' cut out of one line, and a detector keyed on one caption per line counts two exhibits where this paper prints four.

One caption is glued to the prose that introduces it and never parses as a token: the p16 line reads 'The two radar charts above show more intuitively the changes of each indicator inFigure 8: The Integrated Value of Kenya', so [caption.verbatim] for Figure 8 is quoted from inside that line rather than read as a standalone line, and the same failure mode swallows 'Figure 8' from any 'Figure 8' search of the text layer.

Every table in the paper is booktabs and every one measures from exactly 3 vector paths - the top rule, the rule under the last header row and the bottom rule - so [table.rule_style] is 'booktabs' on all five rows and rule_tables are recognisable here only by that three-path signature, with no interior or vertical rule anywhere in the paper.

Only Table 3 is a numeric matrix: 5 columns, 2 header rows, Greece and Kenya spanning two columns each, four columns of fixed three-decimal values and one label column, so [table.header_rows] is 2 and [table.numeric_cols] is 4 on that row alone. The other four tables append the percentage inside the label cell ('Food Species 2.3%', 'Food Packing 3.8%'), which is why [table.numeric_cols] is 0 on them and their item counts sit in [table.text_cols] instead.

The five tables print only TWO titles between them: Tables 1, 2 and 3 all print 'The weights of Basic Food Systems indicators' over three unrelated tables (a three-block weight split, an Efficiency/Emergency split, and the Greece/Kenya basic-versus-optimised matrix), and Tables 4 and 5 both print 'The modified weights of Food Systems indicators' - so [caption.verbatim] repeats across rows and the printed title can never be used to tell one table from another.

Families over the sixteen figures: 7 line, 4 flowchart-or-schematic, 2 node-link-network, 2 other, 1 bar. The two 'other' rows are the radar pair Figures 7 and 8, recorded as 'other' because the closed family vocabulary has no radar key, and [geometry.legend] is 'below' on both because the only key is the two-swatch block printed under the plot.

The radar family also fails the number test: neither radar prints a scale ring, a tick or an axis value, so [geometry.printed_numbers] is false on Figures 7 and 8 while it is true on every line and bar figure that carries ticked axes - the printed values there are free floating numbers whose series membership cannot be read off the drawing.

Three figures are schematics with no quantity at all - Figure 1, Figure 3 and Figure 4 - and one is drawn in pseudo-3D: Figure 11's two cut-away blocks are extruded in isometric projection, so [geometry.three_d] is 'isometric' on that row alone and 'no' on all others, while [geometry.printed_numbers] is false on all four because none of them prints a number.

Panel count is per image, not per printed grid: Figure 6 draws THREE lettered bar panels A, B and C inside one raster on a shared y axis, so [geometry.panel_count] is 3 with layout '1x3' on that row and 1 everywhere else, including the caption-sharing pairs, where each country keeps its own image and its own panel.

Citations are twelve pointer lines in the whole paper and only four of them name a number: 'Figure 1' on p3, the ligature spelling 'figure 2' on p4, and 'Table 2' twice on p16 - the last of which is a mis-pointer, because the sentence describes the Greece/Kenya Basic-versus-Optimization comparison that only Table 3 holds. So [mention.count] is 1, 1 and 2 on those three rows, [mention.style] carries the spelling actually printed (including the lower-case ligature form), and thirteen of the twenty-one exhibits are never cited.

Eight further pointer lines name no number at all - 'the figure shows', 'the following figure', 'the table shows' - and are counted only when the page they sit on carries exactly one exhibit (Figures 5, 11, 15 and 16, [mention.count] 1 each, [mention.style] the bare word actually printed). The other four sit on p4, p16, p20 and p22, where no number and no position identifies the exhibit, and are counted for none rather than guessed onto a row.

Printed defects are recorded per row: 'Intronational', 'E-bussiness' and 'Retailor' in Figure 3, 'Transpotation' twice plus 'Mraket Information' and 'Lanscape' in Figure 15, 'Transporta tion' and 'Sustaina bility' as broken words, the y title of Figure 5 set as 'GT CO2,e q', Figure 6 with no x axis line or title and error bars on some bars only, Figures 13 and 14 drawn as two rasters that OVERLAP by 33.1 pt, '0. 197' with a stray space inside the number in Figure 8, and the paper's watermark printing through the box of Table 5, which is why [geometry.printed_numbers] is false on the two radar rows and true on the ticked ones.
